title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is grappling with a mix of operational challenges and strategic developments. From bankruptcy filings to new launch plans, the sector is anything but dull.

themes.title: Drones and Launch Safety
themes.body: The increasing presence of drones near U.S. rocket launch sites raises significant safety concerns. As the threat landscape evolves, the industry must adapt to ensure secure operations.

themes.title: Financial Turbulence in Space
themes.body: EchoStar's bankruptcy filing underscores the financial pressures facing satellite operators in a competitive market. Meanwhile, Palantir's contract extension hints at ongoing government reliance on established tech players.

themes.title: New Launch Initiatives
themes.body: Latitude's upcoming launch from Oman signals a diversification of launch sites, potentially easing congestion at traditional locations. Blue Origin's revised launch pad strategy aims to bring New Glenn back into the fray, but the timeline remains uncertain.

themes.title: Defense and Space Integration
themes.body: The Space Force's integration with the Air Force highlights a growing emphasis on AI to bolster mission capabilities. As defense tech lobbying ramps up, the intersection of space and military readiness is becoming a focal point.
